name: Apache Kafka
description: Protects against destructive Kafka CLI operations like deleting topics, \ removing consumer groups, resetting offsets, and deleting records.

destructive_patterns.name: kafka-topics-delete
destructive_patterns.description: kafka-topics --delete removes Kafka topics and data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Kafka topic permanently removes all messages and partitions. \ Consumers will receive errors, and any unprocessed data is lost. Producer \ applications may fail until they handle the missing topic.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kafka-topics --describe: Review topic details first \ - Set retention.ms to expire data naturally \ - Back up critical data before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: kafka-consumer-groups-delete
destructive_patterns.description: kafka-consumer-groups --delete removes consumer groups and offsets.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a consumer group removes all committed offsets. When consumers \ reconnect, they will start from the earliest or latest offset based on \ their configuration, potentially reprocessing or skipping messages.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kafka-consumer-groups --describe: Check group status first \ - Reset offsets instead of deleting the group \ - Ensure all consumers are stopped before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: kafka-consumer-groups-reset-offsets
destructive_patterns.description: kafka-consumer-groups --reset-offsets rewinds offsets and can cause reprocessing.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Resetting consumer offsets can cause messages to be reprocessed or skipped. \ This affects data consistency if your consumers are not idempotent. Resetting \ to the earliest offset on a high-volume topic may trigger massive reprocessing.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use --dry-run to preview the reset first \ - Reset to a specific timestamp or offset for precision \ - Ensure consumers are stopped before resetting

destructive_patterns.name: kafka-configs-delete-config
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting configuration overrides reverts topics or brokers to default \ settings. This can unexpectedly change retention, replication, or \ compression behavior.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kafka-configs --describe: Review current configuration first \ - Set explicit values instead of deleting to revert to defaults \ - Test configuration changes in a non-production environment

destructive_patterns.name: kafka-acls-remove
destructive_patterns.description: kafka-acls --remove deletes ACLs and can break access controls.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing ACLs can immediately break access for producers and consumers. \ Applications may fail with authorization errors, causing message loss \ or processing delays.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - kafka-acls --list: Review existing ACLs first \ - Test ACL changes in a non-production environment \ - Add new ACLs before removing old ones during transitions

destructive_patterns.name: kafka-delete-records
destructive_patterns.description: kafka-delete-records deletes records up to specified offsets.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
This command permanently deletes messages from topic partitions up to the \ specified offsets. Deleted data cannot be recovered. Consumers attempting \ to read deleted offsets will encounter errors.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use retention policies for automatic data expiration \ - Verify the offset JSON file carefully before execution \ - Consider topic compaction for key-based retention

destructive_patterns.name: rpk-topic-delete
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a topic via rpk (Redpanda) permanently removes all data and \ partitions, similar to kafka-topics --delete. This affects both Redpanda \ and Kafka-compatible systems.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - rpk topic describe: Review topic details first \ - rpk topic list: Verify the topic name \ - Use retention settings for data lifecycle management
